title: dockato: water onto DMSO (docked molecule with ROT groups)
purpose: `dockato` [@epsrmanual] builds larger molecules from `.ato` building blocks: copies of the first molecule of a docking file are bonded onto free sites of a docked file, removing one atom of each to form the new bond. Here the docked molecule already has rotational groups, which must be shifted when a new group is inserted.
fortran: `dockato.f`: `dockato` (driver, parameters from command line or stdin), `rotatem`, `random_rotatem`, `search_unsaturated`, `find_valence`
system: Building blocks of EPSR-test: `DMSO.ato` (one DMSO, (CH3)2SO, S-C 1.82 Å, C-H 1.10 Å, two methyl ROT groups) and a water molecule. Atom `atomd` of the new molecule is placed on `atomv`, the molecule is rotated so that its `atomdr` neighbour lies on the `atomvr` neighbour of `atomv` (equal bond lengths required), an optional second (dihedral) rotation about the new bond uses `atomdrr`/`atomvrr` (random angle in [dminrr, dmaxrr] from `ran1`, the Park-Miller generator with Bays-Durham shuffle [@parkmiller1988,@numrec1992], or a fixed dihedral that creates a DIH group when dminrr = dmaxrr), overlaps are tested with a distance factor, `atomd` and `atomvr` are removed and the new rotational group, bonds and atom types are updated. The water H1 is docked onto a DMSO C and its O1 onto the C-H hydrogen, forming a C-O bond (a methoxy-like substitution of a methyl H); the existing DMSO ROT groups are shifted and a new ROT or DIH group is inserted.
inputs: `WaterOH110.ato` = `WaterMolecule.ato` with the O-H bond entries set to 1.10 Å (coordinates unchanged), because the two site pairs need equal bond lengths. Run 1: site answers `C H H`, 30-90°, factor 1.0 from `dmso_random.stdin`, 3 molecules; run 2: fixed dihedral 180° referenced to S, overlaps allowed, 4 molecules; run 3: no second rotation, factor 0.9, 6 molecules.
verification: Each run writes one new `.ato` file (coordinates, bonds, rotational groups, atom types and the random-number state), compared byte for byte with the stored Fortran output. Outputs: `dmsowater.ato` 13 atoms (3 dockings) with 5 ROT groups; `dmsodih.ato` 14 atoms with 2 ROT + 4 DIH groups; `dmsonorot.ato` 16 atoms (6 dockings) with 2 ROT + 6 DIH groups.
